Package com.tencent.tcr.sdk.api.data

Class StatsInfo

java.lang.Object
com.tencent.tcr.sdk.api.data.StatsInfo
public class StatsInfo extends Object
Performance statistics information class

This class encapsulates real-time performance metrics in cloud gaming sessions, with data sourced from WebRTC's RTCStatsReport. These metrics are used to monitor network quality, video stream performance, audio stream performance, and remote device resource usage.

  • Field Details

    • cpu

      public String cpu
      Remote device CPU usage

      Represents the CPU usage of the cloud game server, formatted as a percentage string (e.g., "45.2"). This value is obtained from the server via heartbeat messages and is used to monitor server performance status.

    • gpu

      public String gpu
      Remote device GPU usage

      Represents the GPU usage of the cloud game server, formatted as a percentage string (e.g., "78.5"). This value is obtained from the server via heartbeat messages and is used to monitor server graphics rendering performance.

    • fps

      public long fps
      Actual rendering frame rate (FPS)

      Represents the actual video frame rate rendered by the client, measured in frames per second. Returns the rendering frame rate from WebRTC statistics (googFrameRateOutput).

      Data source: WebRTC Legacy API (googFrameRateOutput)

    • edge_rtt

      public long edge_rtt
      Round-trip time (RTT) measured by edge server

      Represents the round-trip time measured by the edge server.

    • raw_rtt

      public long raw_rtt
      Raw round-trip time (RTT) measured by STUN binding request/response

      Represents the network round-trip time measured via WebRTC STUN protocol, in milliseconds (ms). This value comes directly from the currentRoundTripTime in WebRTC's candidate-pair statistics, reflecting the network latency between the client and the STUN server.

    • rtt

      public long rtt
      Round-trip time (RTT) measured by application layer heartbeat request/response

      Represents the round-trip time measured via application layer heartbeat messages, in milliseconds (ms). This value reflects the complete time from sending a heartbeat request from the client to receiving the server response, including both network transmission latency and server processing latency.

      Note: This value is typically larger than raw_rtt because it includes application layer processing overhead.

    • bitrate

      public long bitrate
      Total audio and video receiving bitrate

      Represents the total bitrate of audio and video data received over the network, in bits per second (bps). This value is calculated from the change in total bytes received between two consecutive statistics: bitrate = (current bytes - previous bytes) * 8 * 1000000 / time interval (microseconds)

    • audioRecvBitrate

      public long audioRecvBitrate
      Audio receiving bitrate

      Represents the bitrate of audio data received over the network, in bits per second (bps). This value is calculated from the change in audio bytes received between two consecutive statistics.

      Calculation formula: audioBitrate = (current audio bytes - previous audio bytes) * 8 * 1000000 / time interval (microseconds)

    • videoRecvBitrate

      public long videoRecvBitrate
      Video receiving bitrate

      Represents the bitrate of video data received over the network, in bits per second (bps). This value is calculated from the change in video bytes received between two consecutive statistics, and is an important metric for measuring video stream quality.

      Calculation formula: videoBitrate = (current video bytes - previous video bytes) * 8 * 1000000 / time interval (microseconds)

    • audioSentBitrate

      public long audioSentBitrate
      Audio sending bitrate

      Represents the bitrate of audio data sent from the client to the server, in bits per second (bps). This value is calculated from the change in audio bytes sent between two consecutive statistics, and is used to monitor the bandwidth usage of the uplink audio stream.

      Calculation formula: audioSendBitrate = (current audio sent bytes - previous audio sent bytes) * 8 * 1000000 / time interval (microseconds)

    • videoSentBitrate

      public long videoSentBitrate
      Video sending bitrate

      Represents the bitrate of video data sent from the client to the server, in bits per second (bps). This value is calculated from the change in video bytes sent between two consecutive statistics, and is used to monitor the bandwidth usage of the uplink video stream (such as camera feed).

      Calculation formula: videoSendBitrate = (current video sent bytes - previous video sent bytes) * 8 * 1000000 / time interval (microseconds)

    • packetLost

      public int packetLost
      Video packet loss count

      Represents the number of video data packets lost during the current statistics period. This value comes directly from WebRTC's inbound-rtp statistics and reflects network transmission quality. High packet loss rates can lead to video stuttering, artifacts, and other issues.

      Data source: WebRTC RTCStatsReport → inbound-rtp(video).packetsLost

      Related metrics:

      • packetReceived: Number of video packets received
      • Packet loss rate = packetLost / (packetLost + packetReceived)

    • packetReceived

      public long packetReceived
      Video packets received count

      Represents the total number of video data packets successfully received (cumulative value). This value can be used together with packetLost to calculate packet loss rate for assessing network quality.

      Data source: WebRTC RTCStatsReport → inbound-rtp(video).packetsReceived

      Note: This is a cumulative value that continues to grow throughout the session duration.

    • videoFreezeCount

      public long videoFreezeCount
      Video freeze count

      Represents the number of video freezes that occurred during the current statistics period. This value is calculated from the increment of freezeCount between two consecutive statistics. WebRTC considers a video freeze when the frame interval exceeds a certain threshold.

      Data source: WebRTC RTCStatsReport → track(video).freezeCount

      Related metrics:

      • videoFreezeDuration: Total freeze duration
      • freezeDuringLast10s: Freeze duration in the last 10 seconds

    • videoFreezeDuration

      public double videoFreezeDuration
      Video freeze total duration

      Represents the cumulative duration of video freezes during the current statistics period, in seconds. This value is calculated from the increment of totalFreezesDuration between two consecutive statistics, and is used to quantify the impact of freezes on user experience.

      Data source: WebRTC RTCStatsReport → track(video).totalFreezesDuration

      Note: This is an incremental value representing the freeze duration within the current statistics period (typically 1 second).

    • framesDecoded

      public long framesDecoded
      Successfully decoded video frames count

      Represents the total number of video frames successfully decoded by the video decoder (cumulative value). This value is used to assess the decoder's working status and the integrity of the video stream.

      Data source: WebRTC RTCStatsReport → track(video).framesDecoded

      Related metrics:

      • framesReceived: Number of video frames received
      • framesDropped: Number of video frames dropped
      • Decode success rate = framesDecoded / framesReceived

    • framesReceived

      public long framesReceived
      Received video frames count

      Represents the total number of video frames received from the network (cumulative value). This value includes both successfully decoded frames and dropped frames, used to assess video stream transmission.

      Data source: WebRTC RTCStatsReport → track(video).framesReceived

      Note: framesReceived = framesDecoded + framesDropped (theoretically)

    • framesDropped

      public long framesDropped
      Dropped video frames count

      Represents the total number of video frames dropped due to various reasons (such as decode delays, buffer overflow, etc.) (cumulative value). Frame drops lead to choppy video playback; the larger this value, the worse the playback quality.

      Data source: WebRTC RTCStatsReport → track(video).framesDropped

      Common causes of frame drops:

      • Insufficient decoder performance
      • Busy rendering thread
      • Network jitter causing uneven frame arrival times

    • nackCount

      public long nackCount
      NACK (Negative Acknowledgement) request count

      Represents the total number of NACK messages sent from the client to the server (cumulative value). NACK is WebRTC's packet loss recovery mechanism; when packet loss is detected, the receiver sends NACK requests to the sender to retransmit lost packets. A larger value indicates more severe network packet loss.

      Data source: WebRTC RTCStatsReport → inbound-rtp(video).nackCount

      Note: The NACK mechanism can recover some packet loss but increases latency. Frequent NACKs indicate poor network quality.

    • lastDecodeMs

      public int lastDecodeMs
      Last video frame decode time

      Represents the time taken to decode the most recent video frame, in milliseconds (ms). This value is used to monitor the decoder's real-time performance; excessive decode time may lead to increased playback latency.

      Data source: WebRTC Legacy API → googDecodeMs

      Related metrics:

      • googMaxDecodeMs: Maximum decode time
      • googFirstFrameReceivedToDecodedMs: First frame decode time

    • codecName

      public String codecName
      Video codec format

      Represents the name of the video codec currently in use, such as "H264", "H265", "VP8", "VP9", etc. This value comes from WebRTC Legacy API statistics and is used to identify the encoding format of the video stream.

      Data source: WebRTC Legacy API → googCodecName

      Note: Different codecs have different characteristics in terms of compression ratio, image quality, and performance. H265 has a higher compression ratio compared to H264, but also has higher decoding complexity.
